title: Washing Dishes After Supper
description: Use warm soapy water and a drying rack after supper.
cardDescription: Use warm soapy water and a drying rack after supper.
focus: The setting is washing Dishes After Supper. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Container from which food is served
Porous absorbent object used for wiping
Small pocket of air in soapy water

answerNotes.SOAP: Soap helps remove dirt when used with water. Rinsing carries away the loosened dirt and remaining suds.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.PLATE: A plate is flatter than a bowl. Its broad surface is useful for separate portions of a meal.
answerNotes.CUP: Cup can name a drinking vessel or a measuring amount. A recipe's measured cup is not simply any small mug.
answerNotes.FORK: A fork's prongs hold pieces of food. A garden fork is a larger tool sharing that pronged shape.
answerNotes.DRY: Dry can be an adjective or an action. It can describe laundry after airing or what happens when moisture leaves a flower bundle.
answerNotes.TOWEL: Towels absorb water after washing or swimming. Their looped fabric holds more moisture than a smooth hard surface.

title: Dusting the Living Room Shelves
description: Wipe fine dust from books, frames, and the shelf beneath them.
cardDescription: Wipe fine dust from books, frames, and the shelf beneath them.
focus: The setting is dusting the Living Room Shelves. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Rub to make a surface shine
Furniture with a flat top and legs

answerNotes.CLOTH: Cloth means fabric. A cloth used for wiping is an object made from that material, not a different substance.
answerNotes.SHELF: A shelf is a horizontal storage surface. A drawer is a compartment that slides in and out.
answerNotes.BOOK: A book has pages joined inside a cover. The title names the work; the author is the person who wrote it.
answerNotes.LAMP: A lamp provides light from a fuel or electrical source. Bible lamps used oil rather than a modern bulb.
answerNotes.FRAME: A frame surrounds and supports an image or object. The glass, backing, and outer border are separate parts of a picture frame.
answerNotes.WOOD: Wood comes from trees and has a grain. Following that grain when sanding usually leaves a smoother surface.
answerNotes.SOFT: Soft describes something that yields to touch. It can refer to cloth, an animal's fur, or food that is easy to bite.
answerNotes.TABLE: A table provides a raised flat surface. Chairs are the separate furniture used to sit beside it.
answerNotes.FEATHER: Feathers help birds with warmth and, in many species, flight. Small soft down feathers have a different job from long wing feathers.

answerNotes.STEP: Step can name an action or one level of a stairway. In a stepping-stone clue, it concerns placing a foot on the next surface.
answerNotes.LEAF: Leaves use light to help a plant make food. The flat blade and its veins are useful details to notice when identifying a leaf.
answerNotes.PAN: Pan is a broad kitchen word. A frying pan is used on a stove, while a loaf pan holds dough or batter in the oven.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
answerNotes.PORCH: A porch is an outdoor entrance area, often with a roof. A patio is usually a paved sitting area at ground level.
answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.
answerNotes.CORNER: A corner is where two edges meet. In a jigsaw, a corner piece normally has two outer edges.

answerNotes.MIRROR: A mirror reflects light to form an image. Cleaning the surface removes marks; it does not change the reflected object.
answerNotes.GLASS: Glass is usually transparent but can also be colored. A glass is a drinking vessel, while glass without an article can name the material.
answerNotes.CLOTH: Cloth means fabric. A cloth used for wiping is an object made from that material, not a different substance.
answerNotes.FRAME: A frame surrounds and supports an image or object. The glass, backing, and outer border are separate parts of a picture frame.
answerNotes.DRY: Dry can be an adjective or an action. It can describe laundry after airing or what happens when moisture leaves a flower bundle.

answerNotes.SHEET: Sheet can name paper, bed linen, or a flat baking pan. The scene tells whether the material is paper, cloth, or metal.
answerNotes.BLANKET: A blanket is a covering used for warmth. A quilt usually has several layers held together with stitching.
answerNotes.CORNER: A corner is where two edges meet. In a jigsaw, a corner piece normally has two outer edges.
answerNotes.FOLD: Folding brings one part of a sheet over another. A crease is the line left by pressing that fold.
answerNotes.COTTON: Cotton is a plant fiber used in many washable household items. Wool instead comes from an animal's fleece.
